Thanks for the information. I saw Hadley's post in the Chloropleth's challenge and I am impressed on the power of R in producing geographic maps. I am using sp a lot in the analysis of spatial data but the maps produced from spplot look "ordinary". I wonder if there are equivalent functions of spplot in ggplot2 where one can add legends, scalebars, ticks, geographic grids,north arrows and other overlays. Since I also work with a lot of shapefiles, I also wonder how ggplot can read and import shapefiles.

Cheers,

Julius Tesoro

messages.author: e53f91d0708becab
messages.subject: Re: spplot/gstat in ggplot2?
parts:
This is how I deal to convert a regular grid (polygons) into a dataframe

grelhaOrd <- data.frame("Id"=as.numeric(row.names(grelha@data)),"Quad"=grelha@data[,1])

#! === Converter SpatialPolygonDF em Dataframe para gráficos ggplot2
grelhamap <- lapply(slot(grelha, "polygons"), function(x) lapply(slot(x, "Polygons"), function(y) slot(y, "coords"))) #! Converte SPDF em List
dfTmp <- list()
for (i in 1:dim(summary(grelhamap))[1]) 
{
  dfTmp[[i]] <- data.frame(grelhamap[i],"Id"=i-1,"Ordem"=seq(1:5))  #! adiciona o código e a ordem das coordenadas à cada linha
}
dfGrid <- do.call(rbind,dfTmp) #! Obtem-se um Dataframe para o ggplot2 a partir do objecto List
dfGrid <- merge(dfGrid,grelhaOrd,by="Id")

Paulo

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: spplot/gstat in ggplot2?
parts: > I wonder if there are equivalent functions of spplot in ggplot2 where one can add legends, scalebars, ticks, geographic grids,north arrows and other overlays. Since I also work with a lot of shapefiles, I also wonder how ggplot can read and import shapefiles.

ggplot2 creates legends and axes for you automatically.

What is a geographic grid?

There is no built in functionality for drawing north arrows.

ggplot2 is built around the notion of layers so it's very easy to add
multiple overlays.

You load shapefiles through the usual R mechanism.

You might want to get a copy of the ggplot2 book...

Hadley
